sources: American Academy of Pediatrics, HealthyChildren.org (sleep, feeding, and media)
CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early. developmental milestones
NHS Start for Life and birth-to-five guidance

sleep.0-3: Many babies this age sleep in short stretches through the day and night, and waking to feed is common. A dark, quiet place to put them down is a common setup.
sleep.4-6: Night sleep often gets longer around this age, and many babies still nap several times in the day. Families often use the same short wind-down each evening.
sleep.7-12: Many babies this age take two or three naps and still wake at night. The same few steps at bedtime are a common way the day ends.
sleep.13-18: Many toddlers this age still need one nap a day, and waking early is common. A familiar bedtime routine is a common way families wind down.
sleep.19-24: Many toddlers this age still nap once in the day, and protesting bedtime is common. Keeping the same wind-down steps is a common approach.
sleep.25-36: Some children this age still nap, and some are giving the nap up. Bedtime resistance is common, and a steady evening routine is a common response.
sleep.37-60: Many children this age have stopped napping. Stalling at bedtime and waking in the night still happen in a lot of families.

food.0-3: Milk feeds, often through the day and night, are how babies this age eat. Hunger often returns sooner than a clock suggests.
food.4-6: Milk feeds are still the food at this age. Many babies start to watch what other people are eating.
food.7-12: Many babies this age are learning to eat soft foods as well as milk, and a mess is part of that. Appetite often changes from one day to the next.
food.13-18: Many toddlers this age eat small meals and turn down foods they liked recently. Eating with the family is a common way meals happen.
food.19-24: Wanting the same few foods, and refusing others, is common at this age. Offering a familiar food alongside something else is a common approach.
food.25-36: Many children this age still prefer a few familiar foods. Meals can be short, and playing with food is common.
food.37-60: Many children this age eat with the family and still refuse some foods. Appetite often goes up and down across the week.

play.0-3: Watching a face, listening to a voice and short awake spells are common play at this age.
play.4-6: Reaching, mouthing objects and time spent on the floor are common play. A spell of play is often only a few minutes.
play.7-12: Banging, dropping and passing objects back and forth are common play. Many babies want the same little game over and over.
play.13-18: Filling and tipping containers, and playing beside other children, are common. Play is often on the move.
play.19-24: Simple pretend play, such as feeding a doll or pushing a toy car, is common. Children this age often play near others more than with them.
play.25-36: Pretend play and very simple games with turns are common. Play can tip into frustration quickly.
play.37-60: Imaginative play and time with other children are common. Games with a few simple rules start to make sense to many children this age.

feelings.0-3: Crying is a main way babies this age say they need something. Settling often comes with holding, feeding or a change of position.
feelings.4-6: Many babies this age are more social, and may fuss when a familiar person leaves. A calm adult close by is a common comfort.
feelings.7-12: Caution around new people, and clinging to familiar ones, is common. Big cries over a small change happen a lot.
feelings.13-18: Big feelings are common, including a short meltdown when a toddler cannot manage something alone. Staying close and calm is a common way adults respond.
feelings.19-24: Tantrums, and wanting to do things without help, are common. A calm adult nearby is a common way the moment passes.
feelings.25-36: Strong feelings about small changes are common. Naming the feeling out loud is a common way adults respond.
feelings.37-60: Many children this age can say how they feel, and a big reaction to disappointment is still common. Time with a calm adult often helps the feeling pass.

talking.0-3: Cooing, crying and going quiet for a familiar voice are common. Babies this age also start to trade sounds back and forth.
talking.4-6: Babbling and turning toward a voice are common. Many babies enjoy hearing the same sounds again and again.
talking.7-12: Babbling with a wider mix of sounds is common, and a first word may appear. Understanding usually runs ahead of the words a baby can say.
talking.13-18: Many toddlers this age say a handful of words and understand far more than they say. Pointing and gestures carry a lot of what they mean.
talking.19-24: Many toddlers this age add words quickly, and phrases of two words are common. Understanding still runs ahead of speaking.
talking.25-36: Short sentences and lots of questions are common. People outside the family often find the speech hard to follow, which is common at this age.
talking.37-60: Many children this age speak in sentences and can tell a simple story about the day. Conversation goes back and forth more easily.

moving.0-3: Lifting the head during floor time and watching things that move are common. Movement comes in short bursts.
moving.4-6: Rolling, reaching and pushing up on the arms during floor time are common. Each baby gets there in their own time.
moving.7-12: Sitting, crawling and pulling up to stand are common, and the timing varies a lot from one baby to another.
moving.13-18: Walking and climbing are common, and so are tumbles. Moving along the furniture often comes first.
moving.19-24: Running, climbing and kicking a ball are common. Stairs are interesting, and a hand to hold is a common way families use them.
moving.25-36: Jumping, running and trying stairs with a hand to hold are common. Balance is still developing.
moving.37-60: Hopping, climbing and riding a trike or scooter are common for many children this age. Coordination is still coming along.

care.0-3: Frequent nappy changes are part of the day. Baths are short, with an adult there the whole time.
care.4-6: Bath time is often a playful part of the day, with an adult there throughout. Nappy changes are still very frequent.
care.7-12: Many babies this age take an interest in getting dressed. An adult still stays within reach for the whole bath.
care.13-18: Wanting to help with dressing and washing hands is common, and it often takes longer that way.
care.19-24: Many toddlers this age want to wash and dress themselves. Nappy or potty timing varies a lot from one child to another.
care.25-36: Interest in the potty is common, and so is a wide range of timing. Accidents are part of this stretch for many families.
care.37-60: Many children this age use the toilet, and accidents still happen. Brushing teeth with an adult helping is common.

outings.0-3: Short trips out, and a lot of time being carried, are common. Many babies sleep on the way.
outings.4-6: Many babies this age like looking around on a trip, and some fuss on the way. Shorter outings tend to go more smoothly.
outings.7-12: Outings often go better when they stay short. Many babies this age want to see what is happening around them.
outings.13-18: Many toddlers this age want to walk some of the way and be carried the rest. A short trip with something to look at is a common outing.
outings.19-24: Wanting to walk, and tiring of a long trip, are common. A familiar toy and something to eat are a common way families keep going.
outings.25-36: Many children this age manage a short outing and find a long wait hard. Saying what comes next is a common way families help.
outings.37-60: Many children this age manage a longer outing when they know the plan. Waiting is still hard for a lot of them.

screens.0-3: Babies this age follow faces and voices close by. Screens are not a usual part of play at this age, apart from a live call with a familiar person.
screens.4-6: Babies this age learn from people and from objects they can touch. Screens are not a usual way to fill play at this age.
screens.7-12: People, voices and objects a baby can handle are still how this age learns. Screen use is uncommon as play.
screens.13-18: Children this age still learn most from people and from play. Screens are still an uncommon way to spend the day.
screens.19-24: Where families use a screen at this age, watching together and talking about it is the common pattern, and it stays brief.
screens.25-36: Many families keep screen time short and shared at this age. Play and conversation still fill most of the day.
screens.37-60: Many children this age watch a screen sometimes. Keeping it brief, with an adult watching too, is a common family pattern.
